headline: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raises $24M for AI sensors
script: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi has raised twenty-four million dollars in seed funding. The money will help it develop AI-enabled image sensors for customers in the United States and elsewhere. An image sensor is a chip that turns light into digital pictures. The nearly five-year-old startup says it has already won design deals with General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon. Its sensors are still under development, and commercial production is planned for 2027. India has committed billions of dollars to build a domestic chip industry. The country hopes to become an alternative manufacturing hub as companies diversify beyond China. Bharat Semi is developing programmable image sensors that combine capture, processing, and AI on one chip. This cuts the need to send visual data to separate processors. The company says this could lower system costs by at least seventy percent. Its first-generation sensors are already being prototyped. More advanced second-generation sensors should reach the prototype stage by mid-2027. The company plans to use the funding to grow its engineering team and bring its sensors to market.
